justification: B reads better. In A2 the Arabic columns are small, dense and ragged, and the numerals and punctuation break oddly (e.g. '٪١٢' and the stray gaps). B2 sets larger, well-spaced Arabic with clean line breaks that matches the English column. B's tables and chart (B3) are crisp and the dark navy bars are strong. B's running headers and 'Page 2 of 3' footers add polish. A's horizontal rules and indented text give clearer section bands, but A's Resolutions list wraps awkwardly.

A uses a serif with Arabic sized to match the English, and its green bands are full-bleed and bold. Its chart legend sits clear of the bars, and the Arabic is well-sized with comfortable line spacing (A2, A3). In B the Arabic is noticeably larger and heavier than the English, which unbalances the columns. B's chart legend overlaps the 2024 bar and its resolutions list has uneven justified spacing (B3). Both have the same mirrored chart title glitch. B's navy bands are tidy and its tables are comparable.

Both are short memos with a navy header band and large empty lower pages. B pairs a serif body with a bold sans heading and spaces its bullets more evenly, so it reads more comfortably (B1). A has a thin rule and a light 'Memorandum' heading that is weaker than its subheading (A1), and its sans body is tighter. B's numbered headings (1, 1.1) add clutter to a memo, but they do give clearer heading levels.

B reads better: its Arabic type is larger, more legible and better matched to the Latin serif, and its two columns are aligned and fill the page evenly (B2). A's body text is small, indented and narrow, and its Arabic is cramped and uneven, leaving gaps in the columns (A2). A's headings are bolder, but the B page layout is cleaner. B's chart uses dark navy bars, and A's blue bars are slightly more distinct. B's table is tidy, though similar to A's (A3, B3). B's top band adds a consistent frame.

A has larger, more legible type, numbered headings and a clear hierarchy. Its tables are compact and read well, with running headers and page numbers. Its notes sit on the same page as the tables, and the page flow is continuous. B has a bold blue cover band, but its type is small and light. B's balance table splits awkwardly across pages (B1-B2), and its notes spill onto a nearly empty last page (B3), leaving an unbalanced layout. A's cover (A1) is plain but clean.

A has a darker navy header band with a larger title that wraps, numbered section headings (1.1, 1.2) and larger body text that is easier to read. B has smaller, lighter text, an orphaned rule, and a one-line title in a brighter blue band. B's smaller text leaves a lot of empty space, and its sections feel less anchored. A's larger text fills the page better, though both leave the bottom empty.

B opens with a strong navy title band and puts the title and first table together on its cover page (B1). Each statement then gets its own page with clean tables and a consistent running header (B2, B3). A's cover is mostly empty, and its tables split across pages: the balance sheet starts on A2 and continues on A3 with no section context. The cramped A2 and A3 are denser, though the numbered headings are clear. B's table cells are tighter and a little less airy, and its last page ends with empty space.

A's title fits on one line in a slimmer blue band, with a clean, consistent type scale and comfortable spacing between sections. B's title wraps and leaves an orphaned word, "المرن", in a heavy green band. B's body text is larger and a bit denser, and its header block is cramped. Both leave empty space at the bottom of the page.

B keeps each statement whole on its own page: the balance sheet is one table on B2, and the cash flow and notes share B3. Its type is larger and easier to read, and it has running headers and footers. A splits the balance sheet across A1 and A2 and leaves a nearly empty A3 holding only notes 2-4. A's table text is small and its rows are loosely spaced, though its header band is attractive. B's cover band is heavy and its title wraps awkwardly, but overall B is more coherent.

A has more generous spacing and clearer separation of the To/From line, with a rule under the banner. Its larger text and looser leading make it easier to read. The banner title in A breaks more gracefully. B is tighter and its numbering ("1 تعميم", 1.1, 1.2) adds clutter. B's title wraps with an orphaned word "المرن", and its body is smaller and justified with uneven gaps.

B has a full green cover, a banded section title, and running headers and footers. Its balance table and notes flow together across pages 2-3, so the last page is full. A splits the balance sheet awkwardly: a heading and two rows sit at the foot of page 1, and page 3 holds only a few leftover notes above a mostly empty page. A's blue header band is clean, but the page breaks are poor. B's tables also split across pages, but less jarringly, and its text is larger and easier to read.

B uses full-width green section bands (B2, B3) that give clear structure and a strong rhythm of section starts. A has plain headings with no bands (A2, A3), so it is cleaner but flatter. B's table and chart share one green accent, which looks more cohesive than A's navy chart. B's two-column body is evenly balanced, and its running headers and footers are more informative. Both charts have a garbled Arabic title, so that does not separate them. A's heading typography is slightly crisper, but B's bands add more visual hierarchy.

A uses navy banded section headings and a running header, so the three sections are easy to pick out (A2). Its bold sans type keeps the English and Arabic well matched. B has a refined serif look, but its thin-rule headings are weaker. B's chart legend overlaps the Q1 bar (B3), and B's Arabic text is slightly more cramped than A's. A's chart has the same legend overlap problem, but it is less severe. A's table and chart are clean (A3).

B's body text is larger, and its list items wrap, so lines are comfortable and fill the column. A's text is small and light, and the lower third of the page is empty, which makes it feel thin. A's navy band is richer and its headings are slightly clearer. B's band is dark slate, and its justified lines show uneven word spacing, as in the 'to/from' line. B's numbered list has more generous line spacing and is easier to scan (B1). Overall, B is more readable and better balanced on the page than A1.

B has a larger body text size and a bigger header band with a two-line title, so its hierarchy is stronger and it is easier to read (B1). A's text is small and light, with a lot of empty space below the content, and its header is thinner with a single-line title (A1). A's spacing is airier, but the text is harder to read. B's size and contrast make it a bit better overall.

A's Arabic is larger and clearer and sits at a similar visual weight to the English, so the bilingual columns read evenly (A2). B's Arabic is small and light, and the English column is indented, which makes the columns uneven and harder to read (B2). A's two-column layout is more balanced and its serif headings are cleaner, with a dark band on top of the pages. B's blue chart is a bit more engaging, and both tables are similar, but A is better overall. Both charts show a garbled Arabic title.

A uses full-width green section bands with white headings (A2, A3), so the sections are clearly separated and easy to scan, and the pattern repeats consistently. B has plain headings with numbering (B2, B3) that are clean but flatter, and the Resolutions heading sits close to the chart. The tables and charts are nearly identical. Both show the same garbled Arabic chart title. B's 'Page 2 of 3' footer is a small plus, but A's stronger structure wins.

B uses larger text with more generous line spacing, so the memo is much easier to read, and it fills the page well. B's headings stand out more clearly and the list items are evenly spaced. A's small, light text leaves the bottom half of the page empty, so the page feels unbalanced and the body is hard to read. A's blue band is attractive, and its title fits on one line. B's title wraps onto two lines, and its text is justified, which makes some word gaps uneven.

A has a full dark green cover page and a green title band on page 2 that give clear structure. Its tables are well proportioned and its notes fit together on page 3. B wastes space: the notes are split so that page 3 holds three short notes and is mostly empty. B's balance sheet table breaks across pages after only two rows, and its small table text is lighter and harder to read.

A uses full-width dark green section bands with white bilingual headings, which give clear hierarchy and a strong rhythm (A2, A3). Its running headers show the section name, and the table has a bold header rule. The body text is larger and more legible. B is clean but plain: thin rules and light headings, a smaller serif body, and weaker hierarchy (B2, B3). Both charts have the same garbled Arabic title, so that does not separate them.

A uses strong green section bands with white headings, so the sections are clear and the hierarchy is easy to scan (A2, A3). Its Arabic text is more legible and well shaped. B's thin rules and small headings are quieter and weaker, and its Arabic body text has odd spacing and gaps around the numerals (B2). The tables and charts are similar in both, but B's chart title and Arabic text render slightly less cleanly. A's Resolutions band is heavy but gives a consistent rhythm.

A sets the Arabic text in a natural face with even word spacing and clean line breaks, so it reads smoothly. B has wide, uneven word spacing in the memo line and paragraph, and the bullets wrap with orphaned words such as "المباشر" and "عن بُعد". Both use a similar header band and heading structure, but A's bands and spacing feel more consistent. Page A1 is stronger than B1.

Scoring note: positive favours A, negative favours B. B uses heavy navy header bands with strong section hierarchy (B2, B3), a header and footer, and Arabic set at a size matching the English, so it reads better and looks more finished. A's Arabic is small and light, its body columns are narrow with an indent, and its thin rules make the sections feel weak (A2). A's elegant serif and generous whitespace are a plus. A's Arabic chart title is garbled in both designs. B's chart legend overlaps the bars, which is a minor flaw. B's table is clean with a highlighted column. B's cover is also comparable.

A combines the cover and table of contents on one page with a navy title band. Running header and footer bands and a filled Recommendations band give strong structure and a consistent rhythm (A1, A2, A6). A packs two charts onto most pages, so the pages feel fuller. B has an almost empty cover, a sparse contents page, and pages 4 and 5 that are mostly blank. B's serif body text is pleasant, but its Summary heading and body are misaligned and indented inconsistently (B3). B's charts are slightly larger and more legible, and its tables are clean, but B lacks bands and its whitespace is uneven.

A uses a consistent serif family with a rule under the band and generous margins. The header line in A runs together in a larger size, but the body reads comfortably. B mixes a sans heading with a serif body and uses justified text with visible gaps in the lines. Its numbered headings ('1 Memorandum', '1.1 Key changes') are unnecessary for a one-page memo. B's hierarchy is clear, but A looks more refined overall. Both leave the lower half of the page empty.

A has larger body text and a taller green band, but its title wraps to leave one orphan word (المرن). The larger type and generous line spacing make A easier to read and better filled. B's title fits on one line in a compact band, but its small, light body text looks thin and leaves the lower half of the page empty. A's section headings and list spacing feel more even.

A gives each statement its own page, so the tables stay whole and the page rhythm is consistent. Its navy header band on A1 is strong, and the running headers and highlighted columns are clean. B has a mostly empty green cover (B1). Its balance sheet splits across B2 and B3, and the split is awkward: a header row is repeated mid-table, and the earlier part ends on a dangling 'non-current assets' row. B's justified paragraph also has uneven spacing. B's cover is elegant, but the broken table hurts it more.

B keeps the balance sheet table together with the cash flow statement and notes, and its running headers and numbered sections give clear navigation (B2, B3). Its tables have even row spacing and the notes are readable in one block. A has a strong blue header band (A1), but its balance sheet table splits awkwardly across pages after only two rows (A1, A2). Its last page is nearly empty, holding only three notes (A3). B's cover page is mostly empty, but it is a deliberate title page (B1).

A has a navy header band with a clear title, numbered section headings (1.1, 1.2), and justified body text with consistent line lengths. B's wide letter-spacing makes Arabic letters look disconnected and harder to read. B's bullets wrap with orphaned words, and its metadata line breaks awkwardly mid-date. B's darker band and rule are fine, but its section headings are less distinct.

A puts a navy title band and the income table together on page 1, then gives each statement its own page with a running header. The tables stay whole and the page footers are clear. B spends a full page on a mostly empty dark cover. It also splits the balance sheet table across pages 2 and 3, leaving only two rows on page 2 and repeating the header on page 3. That break hurts reading, and page 4 holds only the short notes.

A uses a clean sans-serif with Arabic and Latin that match well, and its navy bands are contained within the margins (A2, A3). B's serif body is heavier and its Arabic is lighter and smaller than the Latin. B's full-bleed green bands are bold but crowd the text, and the legend in its chart overlaps the Q1 bar (B3). A's chart legend also sits slightly awkwardly, and both charts have a garbled Arabic title. A's body text is lighter and its Arabic is bolder and larger, so the two scripts balance better.

A uses a clearer Arabic typeface with legible digits and bullets. Its body text is slightly larger, and the numbered list sits well. B's lighter, thinner type is smaller, and its bullets look like tiny dots. The title band in B is a little more cohesive, but A's body is easier to read. Both layouts are nearly identical otherwise, with a large empty space at the bottom of the page.

B is more compact: it fits the document on 3 pages with a green title band on B2 and running headers. Its tables sit together, and the notes follow on the same page as the cash-flow table (B3). In A, the balance sheet table splits awkwardly across A2 and A3, and A4 is mostly empty with only four notes. B's balance sheet also splits across B2 and B3, but less awkwardly. A's heavier headings give clearer hierarchy, but its row wrapping is cramped (A2), and its Arabic numerals feel less consistent. B reads more cleanly and has a stronger band.

Design A has a clean green header band, a rule under it, and unnumbered headings. Its body text is cleanly spaced and the lists are easy to scan. Design B adds odd heading numbers ("١ تعميم", "١.١"), which are redundant and clutter a short memo. Its justified paragraph also leaves uneven word gaps. B's bold To/From labels do help a little. Overall A reads as the cleaner memo.

Both are one-page Arabic memos with a colored header band and the same content. A justifies the body text, which opens uneven word gaps in the intro paragraph. A also numbers its headings (1.1, 1.2) after a numbered title, which is slightly awkward, but it gives clearer section structure. B has a rule under the band, a left-aligned ragged intro, and cleaner headings. B reads more naturally, though it is slightly less hierarchical.

B's header band is compact and the title fits on one line, so the page feels more balanced. B also spaces its sections more generously: the bullets and numbered steps are loosely set with clear gaps between groups. A's two-line title in a tall band is heavy, and its body text is tighter and slightly smaller, so the sections feel cramped. A's headings are legible, but B's rhythm is more even.

Both are short memos with a dark header band and empty lower half. B's serif type, left-aligned body and more generous line and bullet spacing read more comfortably. A's justified header line (To/From/Date/Re) has stretched word gaps, and its tighter spacing feels cramped. B's metadata line is larger than its body, which is slightly odd, but overall it is more even.

B puts the title band and the income statement together on page 1, so the first page is useful. Each statement gets its own page in B, and the notes follow the cash flow table without a split. A spends page 1 on a mostly empty dark cover. Its balance sheet splits across pages 2 and 3, so the table header repeats and the 'Current assets' section ends up orphaned from its rows. Its notes page is mostly empty. A's tables are airy and legible, though, and its cover is stylish.

A pairs a serif body with bold sans headings, numbered 1 and 1.1, so the section levels are clear and the text is easy to read. In B the 'Memorandum' heading is light and barely stands out from the body, and the thin body text is weaker. B's rule under the band is a nice touch, but its hierarchy is flatter. Both leave the lower half of the page empty.

A keeps one consistent left margin: the title, rule, heading and body all align at x=75, and the right edge matches. B has a ragged alignment. Its 'Memorandum' heading and rule start at the far left, the body is indented, and the rule extends past the body's right edge, so the page looks lopsided. A's navy band is also calmer than B's saturated blue band, and its serif-free type is cleaner. A's 'Memorandum' heading is light and slightly weak, but this is a minor flaw next to B's misalignment.

B keeps one left margin: the header text, rule, headings and body all share the same edge. In A the 'Memorandum' heading and rule sit at a different left edge than the indented body and header title, and the rule runs past the right text edge. A's header block also runs together as one line with an awkward 'Re:' wrap, and its justified body shows loose word gaps. B has similar justification gaps in the header line but is more consistent overall. B's single sans family reads cleanly, while A's heading-sans and serif body pairing feels less cohesive.

B keeps each statement whole: the balance sheet sits intact on B2 and the cash flow statement with notes on B3. A splits the balance sheet across A2 and A3, which hurts a financial reader. A also has a stark cover (A1) and a green band on A2, but the cover is mostly empty. B's tables are tighter with clearer total rules and a light column highlight. A's rows are airier and A has a pleasant serif-like face. B has a modest weakness: the title band merges the cover with the first statement, but it is compact and effective. B's notes are justified and slightly stretched, and some header cells wrap.

A uses larger body text with comfortable line spacing, so it reads more easily and fills the page more evenly. Its numbered list is clear and its bullets wrap cleanly. B's body text is small and tight, and the lower third of the page is left empty. B's header band is a brighter blue with white text, which is slightly punchier, but that does not outweigh its small text.

A's Arabic text is larger, well shaped and easy to read, with numbered headings (1, 2, 3) and a clear running header and footer (A2, A3). B's Arabic is small and thin, with odd gaps around numbers and punctuation such as '١٢    لتبلغ', which hurts readability (B2). B's blue rules above sections add structure, but its headings are weaker and the English text is indented unevenly. Tables and charts are similar in both, but A's table text is more legible (A3 vs B3).

A keeps a clean hierarchy. A thin rule separates the header band from the body, and the headings are clear and unnumbered. The title breaks more evenly across its two lines. B adds numbering such as '١ تعميم' and '١.١', which is unnecessary in a memo, and the numerals are awkwardly placed. B's justified paragraph also shows uneven spacing, and its title wraps with the single word 'المرن' alone on the second line. A's body text is a little small, but it reads cleanly.

A opens with a blue header band, title and subtitle on the first content page, so the content starts at once. Its tables are compact with light row rules and shaded columns, and it has clear section headings. B spends a full page on a dark cover that is mostly empty, and its wrapped table headers and row labels make the tables looser. A has a nearly empty last page, but so does B. B's notes are justified with uneven word gaps, which hurts readability slightly. A splits the balance-sheet table across pages, and B does too.

B reads as the more finished report. Its header and footer bands, numbered headings and consistent margins give clear navigation (B2-B8). A has no bands and its Summary heading and rule sit at a different left margin from the body text, which breaks alignment (A3, A8). A's recommendations list sits tight against the table, and its tinted charts are a little lighter. B's cover is centred and A's is left-aligned, which is a matter of taste. B's thicker bands add some weight, but they also give each page structure.

B is more compact and consistent. Its navy cover band, running header and footer bands, and Recommendations banner (B6) give it structure. It pairs related sections on a page (B3, B4, B5), so pages are fuller and the rhythm is steadier. A spends 8 pages with a sparse cover (A1) and a mostly empty contents page (A2), and leaves large empty areas on A4 and A5, where each page holds a single chart. A's serif body with sans headings is elegant, but its Summary and Recommendations headings are offset from the other headings (A3, A8). B's NPS gauge overlaps the 47 label slightly (B6), a minor flaw.

B uses full-width green section bands with white bold headings, so the sections stand out clearly (B2, B3). Its running headers and footers show the section name in both languages. Its body text is larger and easier to read. Its table has a green tint on the highlighted column and a clear green header rule, and the chart colours match the bands (B3). A is elegant but flat: thin rules and small text make the page look sparse, and the near-black chart is less lively (A2, A3). In both designs the Arabic chart title is garbled, and B's is slightly worse. Overall B's hierarchy and rhythm are stronger.

Design B uses bold full-width green section bands with clear Latin and Arabic headings, running headers and footers, and larger, more readable body text in a balanced two-column layout (B2, B3). Its table and chart are consistent in colour and its resolutions are neatly set. Design A is more restrained, with thin rules and smaller text. It leaves wide gaps between the Latin and Arabic columns and has loose headings (A2). Its two-tone chart is better differentiated, and its Arabic text is a bit cramped. Overall B feels more cohesive and more legible, though its identical-green chart bars make the 2024 and 2025 series hard to tell apart.

B has bolder numbered headings, a running header and 'Page 2 of 3' footer, and a stronger navy chart. Its text columns are larger and more legible, and its table rules are clear (B2, B3). A has a more elegant serif and airy rules, but its body text is smaller and its Arabic is cramped. Its chart is dark and flat, and the heading hierarchy is weaker (A2, A3). Both charts have a garbled Arabic title.

A uses navy header bands for its section titles (A2, A3). This gives clear hierarchy and strong rhythm, and the Arabic text is larger and easier to read. B has plain headings with numbering, a serif body face that sits awkwardly beside the Arabic, and smaller Arabic text. B's chart is slightly cleaner, with an inside legend and more gridlines, and its table is comparable to A's. A's chart legend overlaps the bars slightly. B's resolutions wrap awkwardly, with the year dropping onto its own line (B3). Overall A is more polished and structured.

A has a full dark cover page and a consistent running footer. Its table headers wrap cleanly and the heavier title gives clear hierarchy. B puts its title band on the first content page, which saves a page but crowds the content. B's table is lighter but still fine. B splits the notes across pages 2 and 3, leaving a lone first note at the bottom of page 2 and a mostly empty page 3. A keeps all four notes together on one page.

A opens with a strong navy header band on page 1 and puts the income statement on that page. Each statement then gets its own page, so no table is split across pages. B has a mostly empty cover page, and its balance sheet breaks mid-table across pages 2 and 3, which hurts readability. B's numbered headings and consistent tables are good, but the split table and the wasted cover weigh more. A's notes are justified, which spaces the words unevenly, but this is minor.

A has bold sans headings with numbered sections, so the hierarchy is clearer and easier to scan (A2). Its body text is larger and the Arabic and Latin blocks sit well together. B's light headings are weaker, though its top band and rules give a refined look (B2, B3). The tables are similar. A's navy chart bars carry more colour than B's near-black ones (A3, B3). B's page-3 resolutions have uneven Arabic line breaks. A's running header with the section name is useful.

Both pages share the same layout: a colored title band, a rule, then a memo with bullets and numbered steps. B uses a more legible Arabic typeface with Arabic-Indic numerals and a larger body size. Its bullets are clear, and the line spacing and list indents are comfortable. A's lighter, thinner type is smaller and harder to read. A's title breaks more evenly across two lines, but its dateline is cramped and its lists are less distinct. B's title wraps with a single orphaned word, 'المرن', on the second line, which is a minor flaw. Overall B reads better.

A has a full-bleed dark green cover and a green band behind the page-2 title, which give strong structure and a clear entry point (A1, A2). Its tables are clean, with a tinted highlight column and good row spacing (A2, A3). B has a plain white cover with a centred title that feels weak (B1). B's numbered headings add some structure, but its title sits without a band and the wrapped header cell 'الربع الثالث ٢٠٢٥' is slightly awkward (B2). A's notes paragraphs wrap more cleanly than B's, whose note 3 leaves an orphan word (B3).

A has larger body text and clearer numbered headings (1.1, 1.2), and its title breaks with a single orphan word but still reads well. Its list markers sit close to the text. B's body text is smaller and its bullets are wide of the text. B's title splits more evenly, but the thin rule and small text make the page feel weaker. A is easier to read and has a stronger hierarchy.

A packs cover and contents into one page with a navy title band, then fills pages with two sections each, so density is steady and the recommendations get a banded heading (A1, A3, A6). B spends a near-empty cover page, and its pages 4 and 5 each hold one chart with more than half the page blank, so the rhythm is uneven (B1, B4, B5). B's numbered headings and serif body are tidy, but its pages are less consistent. A's justified text has some wide word gaps, and its TOC page leaves the lower half empty.

A keeps one consistent left margin: the rule, Memorandum heading, body and bullets all align with the title. The serif body pairs well with the dark navy band. B has misaligned edges: the Memorandum heading and rule sit left of the indented body, and the rule runs off-centre toward the right. B's justified text also leaves uneven word gaps, and its bright blue band is heavier. A's header block is a little cramped, but it is more orderly overall.

B uses full-width navy bands for section headings (B2, B3), giving clear hierarchy and strong rhythm. Its header bar is also more distinct. Its Arabic and Latin text sit at a better matched scale in a single sans family, though the Arabic runs slightly larger. A's serif body is neat, but its plain headings feel weaker and the Arabic text is smaller. A's chart legend sits clear of the bars, while B's legend overlaps the plot area slightly. Both mirror the Arabic in the chart title, which renders reversed.

A fits the content on 3 pages and has a green title band on A2 and a clear green cover (A1). Its tables flow with highlighted columns and clean rules (A2, A3). B splits the balance sheet across pages B2 and B3, leaving the balance table broken after only two rows. B's notes page B4 is mostly empty. B's cover title wraps awkwardly, leaving the year alone on a second line.

A uses a larger body size and comfortable line spacing, and its headings are clear. Bullets and numbered steps are well spaced, and the page is filled more evenly. B's body text is smaller and tighter, and its bullets fit on single lines but leave the lower page emptier. B's green band is attractive, but its title wraps awkwardly, leaving the single word 'المرن' on a second line, and A's title wraps the same way. A's header block is slightly less well balanced because its date line wraps awkwardly across two lines, while B keeps it on one line. Overall A is more readable.

B is more compact: the cover and table of contents share one page, and charts are grouped two per page (B3, B4, B5), so pages are fuller and the rhythm is steadier. The navy Recommendations band on B6 adds a strong anchor. A spends a whole page on a nearly empty cover (A1), and A2 and A4 are mostly blank. A5 holds a lone pie chart on a mostly empty page. A's numbered headings and serif body are refined, but its page flow wastes space. B's NPS gauge label overlaps the needle slightly (B6), a small flaw.

A's header band is compact and the title fits on one line, so it reads cleanly. A's headings, body and list items are spaced evenly with a thin rule under the band. B's title wraps and leaves 'المرن' alone on the second line, which looks awkward. B also has odd numbering like '١ تعميم داخلي' and '١.١', which adds clutter, and its justified body text is tighter. B's larger text is a little easier to read, but A looks more polished overall.

B packs content into 3 pages with numbered sections, running headers, and a continuous flow. Its tables are cleaner and only split once, with the notes following directly after the tables. A's dark cover is striking, and its balance of whitespace is decent. But A leaves page 4 mostly empty for four short notes. It also splits the balance sheet awkwardly across pages 2-3, so the tables feel less cohesive. B's numbered headings give a clearer hierarchy, and B's cover is simple and centered.

B keeps a single left margin: the heading, memo line, body and bullets all align with the title in the band. A's "Memorandum" heading and rule sit outdented from the indented body, and its rule runs off-center to the right, which looks misaligned. A's header line runs To/From/Date/Re together in larger text with a different leading, so it reads unevenly. B's numbered headings (1, 1.1) are somewhat bureaucratic, but they are consistent and give a clear hierarchy. Both pages leave the bottom half empty. B's band is a calmer navy and its spacing is more even.

A has a consistent navy header and footer band on every interior page, numbered headings, and running section titles, so it feels more structured and navigable (A2-A8). B is cleaner and has a lighter, slightly more readable serif, but its summary page is misaligned: the heading and rule sit left of the margin while the body is indented (B3, B8). B's centered title is also off-balance. A's cover is centered and tidy (A1). A's table and charts are comparable to B's.

A uses bold navy section bands with a running header and larger Arabic text, so it is clearer and easier to read (A2, A3). B's Arabic is small and light, its thin rules give weak hierarchy, and the body text is dense (B2). The tables and charts are comparable, but A's bold Arabic labels read better. A's chart legend overlaps the bars slightly, and the mirrored Arabic chart title appears in both designs.

B has a full-bleed green cover and a green title band on page 2, which give it stronger structure and identity (B1, B2). A's cover is plain white with a small rule, and its numbered headings are more generic (A1, A2). The tables are nearly identical in both, with shaded current-period columns and clean rules. B's note text wraps more cleanly (B3). A's section numbering helps navigation slightly, but B's band makes the page hierarchy clearer.

A aligns the heading, body and band title on one left margin, with numbered headings that give a clear hierarchy and consistent spacing. B is misaligned: the 'Memorandum' heading and rule sit at the far left while the body is indented, and the rule runs off-center toward the right edge, leaving the right margin uneven. B's saturated blue band is also harsher, and its body text is a bit small.

Design A gives each statement its own page, with running headers and footers and a clear header band. Its tables are compact, with a visible highlighted column and bold total rules (A1, A2). The notes sit under the cash flow table on the same page (A3). Design B splits the balance sheet and cash flow tables across pages and leaves an orphaned header row and two rows at the bottom of B1. Notes split across B2 and B3, leaving B3 almost empty. B's text is smaller and its row spacing looser, so the tables run long and the page rhythm is weaker.

B uses one consistent serif family with left-aligned text, a navy band and rule that match the content width, and even paragraph spacing. A mixes a sans heading with serif body, and its justified paragraph opens wide word gaps. In A, 'Memorandum' sits flush left while the body is indented, and the rule runs wider than the text block, which looks misaligned. A's bright blue band is bolder, but B is more cohesive.

A fits the content onto three pages with numbered section headings (1, 1.1, 1.2) and a running header. The balance sheet continues across pages with its header row repeated, and the notes sit under the cash flow table. B spreads the content over four pages and splits the balance sheet awkwardly after two rows on B2. B4 is mostly empty. B has no section numbers and a weaker hierarchy. B's dark cover band is stronger than A's plain cover, but its heading wraps awkwardly.

A has larger, darker body text and a tall navy header band with a clear title, and the page is well filled. B's body text is small and light, its header band is cramped, and the bottom 30% of the page is empty. A's lists have clearer spacing and larger numerals, though its memo line wraps awkwardly. B is cleaner in places but weaker overall.

A uses a serif face with a larger, clearer meta line and more generous spacing between paragraphs and bullets. B's meta line is justified, which leaves wide gaps between words, and its tighter spacing makes the page feel more cramped. Both pages are mostly empty below the text, with the same header band.

A pairs sans headings with a serif body, so the numbered headings '1 Memorandum' and '1.1 Key changes' stand out clearly from the text. B's 'Memorandum' heading is light and weak, and its header line is larger than the heading. B's justified body has a hyphenation break ('per-mitted'), and its meta line is oversized compared with the body. Both leave the lower half of the page empty, and both have similar banners. A's justified text has some wide word spacing in the meta line, but overall it reads more cleanly.
